title: Summoning
paragraphs: “There should be no one left who can eavesdrop, not even on whispers.”
“Now, I’ll use wind magic to block out all sound.”
“Understood. I shall prepare it on my end as well. Buhuhu… So, what is this about?”
The Pig King’s interest seemed to have peaked considerably. One of the minister-like figures stepped forward, as if to raise an objection.
“Your Majesty! You must not heed the words of such a suspicious Hero—”
Before he could finish, the king merely glanced at his soldiers, and the minister-like man was immediately restrained.
“Dismiss him. He seems suspicious.”
“Y-Yes, Your Majesty!”
With a loud clatter, the minister-looking man was dragged away.

Just one sentence, and he was out of a job? Well, that’s what happens when you fail to read the room. It’s only natural for someone who dares to call a Four Cardinal Hero suspicious to meet such a fate. Most likely, he was a Takt supporter who sensed something was amiss.
“Now then.”

Inside the soundproofed space, where even the wind magic prevented any noise from escaping, I took extra precautions by using magic myself to forcibly mute our surroundings before whispering to the Pig King. His eyes widened in shock.
…Success.
“Of course, Your Majesty is free to be skeptical. But first… we must present evidence, must we not?”

--- That night. Apparently, official duties in Faubrey extended into the nighttime as well. Though the audience itself had ended by evening. King Faubrey, intrigued by my words, had postponed his nightly amusements. He even mentioned finishing up all his pending work. Before long, we were led to a guest room in the castle, where messengers from Takt repeatedly came, persistently trying to reach us. The moment we foolishly approached, they would unleash a barrage of attacks.
“Lord Takt wishes to host a welcome party for the Four Cardinal Heroes and also extend his apologies for the incident earlier today. We humbly request your presence.”
“I refuse. If he wants to apologize, he should come himself. Besides, King Faubrey also stated he had matters to discuss regarding today’s events.”

Takt’s so-called welcome party was being held in a town located within the royal compound beyond the courtyard, where members of the royal family resided. However, since King Faubrey had summoned us, it was only proper for Takt to come to us instead. When Ren was the first to decline, the messenger reluctantly withdrew.
“He really came, huh?”
“Yeah. It’s not that I doubted Motoyasu, but I didn’t think they’d be that blatant about it.”
“But if we hadn’t known, wouldn’t we have reluctantly gone?”
“They say battles are about quality, quantity, and strategy.”
“So, they lured us in with strategy, then planned to ambush us with sheer numbers once we foolishly walked into their trap?”
“When you see through it, it all looks so ridiculous.”
“That’s true. By the way, King Faubrey, what do you think?”
“What do I think…?”
“I felt like my chastity was in danger…”

Indeed, the way they were looking at Ren and Itsuki was disturbing. They were obviously being targeted. And it wasn’t just their problem—this concerned me too. After all, the Pig King was eyeing Yuki-chan and the others intensely.
“Father, are you sure it’s safe to be working with a king like that?”
“I’m starting to feel uneasy as well…”
“Hmm, I’ve only spoken to him a little, so I can’t say for sure, but I think he’s sharper than he looks. Especially in certain areas.”
“You mean in schemes and conspiracies?”
“Exactly. More importantly, look at his age and the state of this country’s public order.”

I’d heard that the Pig King was quite old. Apparently, even older than that scum. As for Faubrey’s public order, since it’s a country of Heroes, I’d heard it was quite stable. I doubt the Pig King governs wisely, so he’s probably left it to his subordinates.
“…So, things are functioning even with him in charge?”
“Thinking back, he’s been spending quite a lot on necessary expenses. It’s been a month since I arrived in this world, but the amount of money involved has been shocking.”
“Yeah. If he were truly an incompetent king, the people would have revolted by now, right?”

That’s true. Like with Melromarc last time, there are cases where the people’s anger boils over. But I haven’t heard of anything like that in Faubrey. At most, in the first world, Takt took over the government. But as far as I remember, Takt was still a minor royal. So, rather than a revolution, it was more like a regime change.
“I see. He’s not an ally, but as long as we don’t make him an enemy, there’s a way to deal with him…”
“That’s why we’re about to demonstrate our usefulness, right?”
“Exactly. Though, he’s definitely a troublesome opponent.”
Father and the others were having that discussion. After a while, another messenger arrived, bringing along some pigs.
“Please, come to the banquet hosted by Lord Takt. You will absolutely make it in time for the welcome party hosted by King Faubrey.”
“Oink!”

“You’re being persistent. It should be your side showing up in person to apologize and make a public appearance! Who do you think you are?! Or are you saying you intend to disregard the Four Holy Heroes?”
This time, Itsuki engaged in a back-and-forth with the messenger. As expected, the messenger was quite persistent.
“He seemed pretty frustrated. He was biting his lip.”
“It’s an obvious trap. At worst, they might try to postpone it until tomorrow.”
“In that case, we’ll just do the same thing. Even if it turns into a game of endurance, we’ll find a way to turn the tables and lure them out instead.”
Once again, a messenger approached us, bringing along multiple of Takt’s pigs. They really are persistent.
“Please, we implore you to come! Lord Takt has expressed great interest in hearing about the illustrious deeds of the Four Holy Heroes!”
“Oink!”
“Oink!”
“Oiiink!”
“For the last time, Takt is just a Seven Star Hero, so he should be the one coming to us!”

Father shouted at the messenger, who was accompanied by the pigs, clearly annoyed. He made sure to emphasize his displeasure. However, the pigs kept oinking obnoxiously. After Ren and Itsuki had their turn arguing, Father continued for a while before the messenger finally realized it was futile and left. And so, the country’s soldiers, under the Pig King’s orders, summoned Takt and his entourage. It seems that Takt, wanting to avoid a direct confrontation with the Pig King, reluctantly complied. We waited with the Pig King in the temple located within the royal harem.
“By order of the king, Lord Takt must come alone.”
“Understood. Damn, what is this all about?”

Before coming here, Takt had apparently ordered several of his women to wait for him at a holding area near the entrance to the royal harem. Right now, we were standing near the king, watching the surveillance system installed throughout the castle—a modified version of the image-crystal technology. I didn’t expect them to have such equipment here. A screen was being displayed through magic. As expected of a technologically advanced nation. Takt walked alone, showing no wariness toward the unnatural separation tactics he himself had often used. His bad luck was meeting an unascended Sakura-chan, her rivals, and—at first glance—a seemingly unimposing Father.
“Takt=Arsahorn=Faubrey, I have answered King Faubrey’s summons!”

Takt had naively walked straight to the temple alone, just as invited. Standing there to receive him were King Faubrey, his royal guards, and us. Well, unlike him, we weren’t foolish enough to launch an immediate ambush. If it were the Father from the first world, he’d probably say:
There’s a much crueler way to handle this. Takt glanced at us briefly before bowing to the Pig King for his audience.
“Bufufufu, welcome, Whip Seven Star Hero… or should I say, that’s not quite right?”
“Hm?”
Takt tilted his head in confusion. But thinking the king was just a foolish pig, he quickly adjusted his expression back to normal. At that moment, Father spoke up.
“Well then, thanks for the entertainment this afternoon.”
